The view through the window of the [Lunar Module](/wiki/Apollo_Lunar_Module "Apollo Lunar Module") *Orion* shortly after [Apollo 16](/wiki/Apollo_16 "Apollo 16")'s landing

A total of twelve [astronauts](/wiki/Astronaut "Astronaut") have landed on the Moon. This was accomplished with two pilot-astronauts flying a [Lunar Module](/wiki/Lunar_Module "Lunar Module") on each of six [NASA](/wiki/NASA "NASA") missions. The missions spanned a 41-month period starting 20 July 1969, beginning with [Neil Armstrong](/wiki/Neil_Armstrong "Neil Armstrong") and [Buzz Aldrin](/wiki/Buzz_Aldrin "Buzz Aldrin") on [Apollo 11](/wiki/Apollo_11 "Apollo 11"), and ending on 14 December 1972 with [Gene Cernan](/wiki/Gene_Cernan "Gene Cernan") and [Harrison Schmitt](/wiki/Harrison_Schmitt "Harrison Schmitt") on [Apollo 17](/wiki/Apollo_17 "Apollo 17"). Cernan was the last man to step off the lunar surface.

All Apollo lunar missions had a third crew member who remained on board the [command module](/wiki/Apollo_command_module "Apollo command module").

Gustave Eiffel engraved on the building of the tower the names of 72 French scientists, engineers and mathematicians as a recognition of their contributions. On 1 July 2023, the merger of HDFC Ltd with HDFC Bank was completed.[[27]](#cite_note-hd4-27)[[28]](#cite_note-hd3-28) Consequently, HDFC Bank had a [market capitalisation](/wiki/Market_capitalization "Market capitalization") of $154 billion, becoming the seventh most valuable bank in the world. HDFC Bank also became one of the [world's top 100 banking companies](/wiki/List_of_largest_banks "List of largest banks") by total assets.[[29]](#cite_note-hd1-29)[[30]](#cite_note-hd2-30)

The combined entity had a customer base of 12 crore (120 million), surpassing the population of Germany in size.[[31]](#cite_note-hd5-31) The merger resulted in a substantial increase in bank headcount, with the workforce totaling 1.77 lakh (177k) employees. The merged entity became the second-largest bank in India, trailing only the [State Bank of India](/wiki/State_Bank_of_India "State Bank of India") in terms of assets.[[32]](#cite_note-hd8-32) The number of branches increased to 8,300.[[33]](#cite_note-hd6-33)

Shares of HDFC Ltd were delisted and shareholders were allotted 42 shares of HDFC Bank for every 25 shares of HDFC Ltd held,[[34]](#cite_note-hd9-34) leading to an increase in the equity capital of HDFC Bank.[[35]](#cite_note-hd7-35)

Four years later, in 1899, Penn's board of trustees voted to retroactively revise the university's founding date from 1749 to 1740 to become older than Princeton, chartered in 1746. Japan as seen from a satellite. Honshu is the largest, middle island.

The island is roughly 1,300 km (810 mi) long and ranges from 50 to 230 km (31 to 143 mi) wide, and its total area is 227,960 km2 (88,020 sq mi).[[1]](#cite_note-honshu-1) It is slightly larger than [Britain](/wiki/Great_Britain "Great Britain"). Its land area has been increasing with [land reclamation](/wiki/Land_reclamation "Land reclamation") and coastal uplift in the north due to [plate tectonics](/wiki/Plate_tectonics "Plate tectonics") with a [convergent boundary](/wiki/Convergent_boundary "Convergent boundary"). Honshu has 10,084 kilometres (6,266 mi) of coastline.[[8]](#cite_note-Britannica-8)

Mountainous and volcanic, Honshu experiences frequent earthquakes (such as the [Great Kantō earthquake](/wiki/1923_Great_Kant%C5%8D_earthquake "1923 Great Kantō earthquake"), which heavily damaged Tokyo in September 1923; and the [earthquake of March 2011](/wiki/2011_T%C5%8Dhoku_earthquake_and_tsunami "2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami"), which moved the northeastern part of the island by varying amounts of as much as 5.3 m (17 ft)[[21]](#cite_note-21)[[22]](#cite_note-Deutsche_Welle-22) while causing devastating tsunamis). The highest peak is the active volcano [Mount Fuji](/wiki/Mount_Fuji "Mount Fuji") at 3,776 m (12,388 ft), which makes Honshu the world's [7th highest island](/wiki/List_of_islands_by_highest_point "List of islands by highest point"). There are many rivers, including the [Shinano River](/wiki/Shinano_River "Shinano River"), Japan's longest. The [Japanese Alps](/wiki/Japanese_Alps "Japanese Alps") span the width of Honshu, from the 'Sea of Japan' coast to the Pacific shore. Western Japan experiences a temperate climate with hot summers and cool to mild winters.
